<TEI xmlns='http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0'><seg xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" type="excerpt" xml:id="ex031012026-09-1508-21-46" status="reviewed">
         <milestone unit="section" n="d"/>
         des na ji skad du lhan cig dmigs pa nges pa'i bsgrub bya tha snyad du med dgag byed na <note type="gloss">tha dad pa'i don bkag pa tsaM sgrub na</note> don byed pas grub pa bsal cing | ma yin dgag byed na <note type="gloss">shes pa'i bdag nyid du grub na</note> dngos mthong med phyir gcig ma yin zhes <note type="gloss"><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:3786">lo tsa</rs></note> bsal ba dgod do zhes <rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:unnamed_reference" ref="db:4207">slob dpon dag</rs> <note type="gloss"><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:4207">me</rs></note><note type="editorial">Tentative identification as </note> <rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:4206">stag</rs><note type="editorial">The gloss can be read as "me stag," referring to two persons, the first being tentatively identified as Me tik pa, who is mentioned above as well (or could also be Me lhang tshe (ID:6655)), the second as rTag pa kha che (ID:4206). However, the reading "me stan" (for "me ston") is also possible, referring in that case to Me dig pa (or me lhang tshe) alone.</note> gsungs <lb edRef="inst:4685" n="13b6"/> ba de rigs par mthong ngo ||</seg></TEI>
